Read the help page (Hand and Crowder; Pinheiro and Bates 2000 App A.3), which gives only the groupedData structure weight ~ Time | Rat; the formula is the book's random-slope fit. Diet is constant within rat.

formula: conc ~ SSbiexp(Time, A1, lrc1, A2, lrc2) + (A1 + lrc1 + A2 + lrc2|Subject)
notes: Read the help page (example nlsList(SSbiexp, data = Cefamandole); Pinheiro and Bates 2000 App A.4). RULE GAP: nonlinear mixed model (biexponential pharmacokinetics); formula is a pseudo-lme4 rendering of the nlme model with random effects on all four parameters, not lme4 syntax.

Read the help page (Vonesh and Carter 1992; Pinheiro and Bates 2000 App A.6); it gives no model. Formula is my recollection of the book's polynomial lme fit in ch. 8, with quartic terms written out; the book also fits a nonlinear model. RULE GAP: model recalled from the book, not stated on the page; the I(pressure^k) terms are not column names, so only pressure and the pressure:QB interaction are declared. index is the within-subject observation number.

Read the help page (Joyner and Boore 1981; Davidian and Giltinan 1995; Pinheiro and Bates 2000 App A.8); it gives no model. Formula is a linearised attenuation model, not verbatim. RULE GAP: the documented model in Davidian and Giltinan is nonlinear in the distance term; soil is left out of the covariates because the page does not say it is in the model.

Read the help page (Lu and Meeker 1993), which has no model, only crack growth of 21 units. Grouping factor Path is documented as the test unit. RULE GAP: crack growth is nonlinear (accelerating) in cycles; the linear formula is a placeholder for the grouping structure.

Read the help page (Prater 1955; Atkinson 1985; Venables and Ripley 2002), whose details say the data are 10 crude oil samples with endpoint a refining characteristic. API, vapor and ASTM are crude-oil characteristics constant within Sample and left out of the covariates. RULE GAP: which covariates the documented model uses is not stated on the page.

Read the help page (Hand and Crowder 1996), which gives no details or model; only a groupedData-style structure is inferred. Meal (6 meal times, ordered) is left out as a covariate. RULE GAP: no formula documented, grouping inferred from Subject.

Read the help page (Hand and Crowder 1996; Pinheiro and Bates 2000 App A.10). RULE GAP: the book fits a nonlinear mixed model to these data; its exact form is not on the page, so the linear formula is a placeholder with the same grouping. Date (2 occasions) is crossed with Subject; only Subject is listed as the grouping factor.

Read the help page (Hicks 1993): 9 teams, each of one physique, each tried both methods twice. Team is nested in Physique; model is the book's fit as recalled. RULE GAP: Physique is a treatment-like 3-level factor used here as a random grouping level.

formula: conc ~ SSfpl(age, A, B, xmid, scal) + (A + B + xmid + scal|Lot)
notes: Read the help page (Davidian and Giltinan 1995; Pinheiro and Bates 2000 App A.11); the page has no model. Four-parameter logistic is the book's nonlinear fit as recalled. RULE GAP: nonlinear mixed model; formula is pseudo-lme4.

Read the help page (Milliken and Johnson 1992; Pinheiro and Bates 2000 App A.14): 6 workers each operate each of 3 machines 3 times; the book's model has a worker-by-machine random term. RULE GAP: the Worker:Machine random factor has no column of its own, so only Worker is listed.
Second model of the book: worker random intercept only, Pinheiro and Bates 2000 ch. 1 (first fit before the interaction term was added).

Read the help page (one row per student, no model); the formula is Raudenbush and Bryk's two-level model fitted in Pinheiro and Bates 2000 sec. 4.3 as recalled. Minority and Sex are not in that model. MEANSES is school-level (constant within School).

Read the help page (Cochran and Cox 1957: roasts in pairs, pairs in blocks, balanced incomplete block design); Pair codes embed the block (II-1), so Pair is a column whose codes do not repeat across blocks. Treatment Storage is fixed. No published fitted model located.

Read the help page (Diggle, Liang and Zeger 1994: protein content after calving under three diets); it gives no model, so a random-intercept longitudinal model is inferred from the described design. RULE GAP: no formula documented, the Time/Diet main-effects structure is my reading.

Read the help page (Baumann and Waldvogel 1963) and the book's nonlinear fit (Pinheiro and Bates 2000 sec. 8.1, exponential decay in conc, recalled). RULE GAP: nonlinear mixed model; formula is pseudo-lme4 with parameters a, b, th.

Read the help page (Bates and Watts 1988), which has no details or model. Grouping inferred from Tissue (4 levels); NIF is a raw-scale copy of log.NIF and is ignored. RULE GAP: the dose-response is nonlinear (sigmoid in log NIF) and only 4 groups; the linear formula is a placeholder.

Read the help page (Yates 1935 split-plot; Pinheiro and Bates 2000 App A.15; Venables and Ripley 2002): 6 blocks, whole plots of Variety, subplots of nitro. Block:Variety (the whole plot) has no column. RULE GAP: random factor as interaction of grouping and treatment columns.
